description: Register a custom eval into the compose critic panel — the critic contract is { rubric (or rules/evaluator), referenceMediaIds?, floor }. Three tiers: rules (declarative constraints — keep-out regions, required elements, max overlays, brand colors), rubric (a text criterion scored by the judge as an extra column), or evaluator (your HTTPS webhook — CueFrame POSTs the composition+stills+facts, you return { score, critique }). referenceMediaIds (≤6 org media ids) attach YOUR reference frames as the standard — the judge scores candidates for consistency with them, so "indistinguishable from mine" is a machine check. Lane scope: rules + rubric critics run in BOTH lanes (the Director's gates AND standalone score_composition); evaluator webhooks run in the Director lane only. Use phase 'static' (the default) — 'temporal' (final-render evaluation) is accepted but not yet wired, so a temporal critic produces no verdicts today. A low client score drives a refine like a built-in criterion. You see your eval output + our scores, never our rubric. Re-registering the same criticId upserts (list_critics / delete_critic manage the set). Evaluator tier returns a signing secret ONCE.

__schema0.description: Stable client id; re-registering the same id UPSERTS.

__schema3.description: Score below this routes a refine like a built-in criterion. Defaults to 6.

__schema6.description: tier "rubric": your criterion + description; scored as an extra column.

__schema7.description: tier "rubric"/"evaluator": up to 6 org media ids whose thumbnails the judge sees as YOUR reference standard — "looks like mine" becomes a machine check. Each must be an org-owned media item with a visual thumbnail (422 names any that is not).

__schema9.description: tier "evaluator": your HTTPS webhook; CueFrame POSTs the artifact.

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.
